answer: One defense is bonded reputation with slashing: each agent must lock a stake before transacting, and its history accumulates like shale layers — cheap to fake once, costly to build thick. A newcomer starts on a low mesa of trust, limited to small trades until peers attest useful work over time. Creating many fake identities then spreads the attacker's stake thin, like a dune shifting under wind: each sybil has too little weight to influence prices or votes, and misbehavior burns its bond, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage.
